svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.aria-label: Five stages. One, the new incident TCK-10562 at Consolidated Messenger, CUST-020, Silver, Fully Managed: dispatchers can't load routes because of a certificate warning; five dispatchers at the north depot see that the routing application's certificate has expired, vans are waiting, and the south depot works; the ticket is New with no priority, category or technician, and it is not in the search index. Two, the agent reads the context: procedure CUST-020-PR3, Dispatch hours, makes a routing outage that stops dispatchers a P2 and says to phone the operations contact; the KB0133 history has 10 tickets, all handled by Daniel Cho, TECH-06, the 7 P2 tickets escalated to the Vendor and 2 of them in a routing application; runbook RB-005 says to find the server and binding and bind the renewed certificate; configuration notes CDOC-032 name the north depot routing server CMRT-N01. Three, the recommendation: Line-of-Business App, Certificate, P2 High with a 16 business hour target, Daniel Cho, TECH-06, escalate to the Vendor and phone Victor Murphy, the operations contact. Four, you approve each write: update_ticket_category, update_ticket_priority, assign_ticket and add_public_reply, each through API Management and the MCP server, on your behalf. Five, each write leaves a correlated trail in Application Insights, API Management, the MCP server log, the Dataverse audit and an Agent Action row, which becomes the evidence for the business case: last quarter 11 Platinum and Gold SLA breaches cost USD 18,400 in service credits.
